summary: Ingmar Heise specializes in sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA in Chinese Studies from Leiden University in 2005 and was attested as a PhD candidate at the University of Bristol in 2012.

Ingo Strauch is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD from the Free University of Berlin in 2000. He held a professorship at the University of Lausanne, attested in 2018, and taught Kathrin Holz.
Inyoung Chung is a scholar of Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at the University of Virginia, where he was attested studying under doctoral supervisor Paul Groner in 2008.

Isabelle Henrion-Dourcy works in Tibetology and related fields. She studied at Tibet University, the EPHE, Harvard University, and the Free University of Brussels, and held posts teaching anthropology at Laval University around 2004 and in 2007.
Isabelle Onians is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed her PhD at the University of Oxford in 2002. She has served as an editor at the Clay Sanskrit Library.

Indologist and philosopher Isabelle Ratié studied at Paris 1, the EPHE, and under Alexis Sanderson. She held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences, Leipzig University, Sorbonne Nouvelle University (2014–2025), and joined the Collège de France in 2025.

Isaline Blew Horner was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Newnham College from circa 1914 to 1917. She served as Honorary Secretary of the Pali Text Society from around 1942 to 1958.

Iselin Frydenlund works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. In 2016, she was attested as a senior researcher at the Peace Research Institute Oslo and as a research fellow at the University of Oslo.

Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at the Sanskrit Collegiate School and Sanskrit College and University. He later served as director of Sanskrit College and University from around 1851 to 1858.
Issaen Ikeyama was a scholar in Buddhist studies who was attested in 1976 as a professor at both Shitennoji Junior College and Eizan Gakuin.
Issei Suzuki was a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at Rissho University and later served as a professor there.
Issei Yamakawa is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at Sophia University and pursued a master's course at Aichi Gakuin University.

Ivan Minayev was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and linguist. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University and under Albrecht Weber, later serving as professor at Saint Petersburg State University and its Faculty of Oriental Studies.
Ives Waldo works in philosophy, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Oxford, studied under Chögyam Trungpa from 1970 to 1988, and taught David P. Jackson.

Ivette Vargas-O'Bryan specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from Harvard University in 2003 under Leonard van der Kuijp, and held a fellowship at Grinnell College.
Ivo Fišer was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He was attested as a lecturer at Charles University in 1960 and at the University of Copenhagen's Institute for Indian Philology in 1970.

Iwao Nakajima studied at Hitotsubashi University and under Nichiki Kimura. Focusing on religious studies and other fields, he worked at the NHK Broadcasting Culture Research Institute until 1975 and was attested as chief editor at Sandhaan in 1999.

Iwao Shima was a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who studied at Nagoya University from circa 1970 to 1979. He held a post at Kanazawa University from around 1989 to 2007, serving as professor from ~2000.

Izumi Hoshi is a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics who studied at the University of Tokyo from 1986 to 1996. Around 2001, she held a post as associate professor at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies.
Izumi Matsuda-Kiami specializes in linguistics and Japanology. She studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, held a post at the University of Washington, and taught Qian Lin.
